title: Every god's light
hook: beaten gods pour out their light, and the light becomes a goddess
carry: shakti is god's power, worshipped as the mother

segments.voice: Last week ended on smriti: Sanjaya remembering the Gita and rejoicing, again and again. A new week, the last of the year, and this one looks forward.

The gods have lost. A buffalo demon, Mahisha, has driven them out of heaven. Led by Brahma, they go to Shiva and Vishnu and tell them everything. And the three great gods, hearing it, grow so angry that light begins to pour out of their faces. Year three on this path was the great story and the saints. Year four is the schools and the goddess, and that scene is its first ridge.
screen: `THE GODS HAVE LOST.` → `LIGHT POURS FROM THEIR FACES.` → `THE SCHOOLS AND THE GODDESS.`

segments.voice: That scene is from the Devi Mahatmya, the Glory of the Goddess. In its second episode, in paraphrase, a great blaze of light streams from Vishnu, from Shiva, from Brahma, and then from all the other gods as well. The light gathers into one mass, like a burning mountain filling the sky. And the mass takes form as a woman. Then each god gives her something of his own. Shiva draws a trident out of his trident and hands it to her. Vishnu brings forth a discus from his discus. One by one, the others give. She laughs, and the world shakes, and she goes out to meet Mahisha. Look at what the story is saying in its own way. The goddess isn't presented as a helper sent by one god. She's what appears when every power is gathered into one, and she can act when the gods themselves couldn't. The tradition's word for that power is shakti. And here's the teaching. For many Hindus, God's power to act is feminine, and is worshipped as the Mother: Durga, Kali, Lakshmi, Saraswati and Parvati, read as faces of one Devi. That's why, at Navaratri, the nine nights of the goddess, families and temples chant this very text and honor her night after night. Later in the same book, the gods praise her as the goddess who lives in all beings as power, and bow to her, again and again. Year four opens with her: the Devi Mahatmya read whole, and Navaratri as a curriculum. This week looks at the ranges beyond her from here, just to know their shape.
screen: `THE GLORY OF THE GODDESS.` · `EVERY GOD'S LIGHT, GATHERED INTO ONE.` · `EACH GOD GIVES A WEAPON.` · `SHAKTI: GOD'S POWER, WORSHIPPED AS MOTHER.` · then, large: `THE FIRST RIDGE OF YEAR FOUR.`

segments.voice: Picture the goddess the way she's shown at Navaratri: many arms, each holding a gift from a different god. With each breath out, bow inwardly and say, silently or aloud, the gods' praise in plain words: to the goddess who lives in all beings as power, I bow, I bow, I bow. If you don't pray, picture the people in your day and bow to the strength in each.
Shakti. Power, energy, and a name for the goddess herself, made when every god's light gathered into one.
Your line: shakti is God's power, worshipped as the Mother. Every god's light, gathered into one. Tomorrow, Shiva's ridge. Same time tomorrow.

howItsDone: The Devi Mahatmya is recited in homes and temples, especially during Navaratri, the goddess's festival; the scene of her forming from the gods' light is painted, sung and acted out.
